answer: A durable defense is stake-backed reputation: each agent locks a deposit that grows only through verified useful work, so its trust signal reflects history, not headcount. A newcomer starts weak and must earn weight slowly, while a detected fake identity loses its stake and its endorsements. One bad actor can spin up thousands of shells, but each shell must pay the same deposit, so the cost ripples across the whole fleet and quickly exceeds any gain. Even a light zephyr of fake accounts cannot sway a vote when weight comes from proven stake and work rather than raw numbers.
